ca_irs_wall.blurb: A small wall in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park, sitting up and to the right of the Dairy Queen Wall. Sixteen routes, almost all trad with a couple of bolted lines, mostly on cracks with a few face climbs mixed in. Roughly a third are easy to moderate leads in the 5.5 to 5.8 range, then a solid block of 5.10s and a handful of 5.11s, so it suits a party with a range of abilities. The wall points mostly northeast, which means early sun and shade by midday. Expect a scrambling walk uphill through boulders from the Dairy Queen approach rather than a roadside crag.

ca_ram_rock.blurb: One of the main formations at Sunset Boulders on the Sonoma Coast, near Jenner. It is a short crag, with rock around 30 feet tall at this site, and most of the sixteen lines here are top-rope problems, plus five boulder problems and a pair of trad leads. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to low 5.11, with the boulder problems spanning easy to quite hard. There is no cover out here: the rocks stand in the open, so a sunny day is pleasant but fog and wind make it chilly. Long slings help when building top-rope anchors, and many routes are best lowered off.

ca_sentinel_west_face_the.blurb: The steep, impressive west side of the big rock fin called The Sentinel, in Real Hidden Valley in Joshua Tree National Park. Of its sixteen routes, fourteen are trad, with one sport line and one top rope, and several are multi-pitch. The rock is solid and clean. Climbing here is mostly serious: nearly everything is 5.10 or harder, with seven routes in the 5.12 range, and only a couple of easier options around 5.8 and 5.9. The face looks west-southwest, so the fin offers shade or sun depending on the face, and this one catches afternoon light. A short trail circles the formation to reach it.

ca_bathroom_boulder.blurb: A single small boulder beside the Castle Lake parking area, above the town of Mount Shasta in northern California, at roughly 5,450 feet. It carries sixteen bouldering problems, with a friendly spread: a handful of V0 and V1 lines, a few V2 and V3, and several harder problems up to V6. The problems are short, around six feet tall in places, so a pad is enough. The boulder sits tucked behind the restroom building, partly hidden by manzanita. At this elevation snow can linger well into late May, so early-season visits may find it buried.

ca_rob_s_rock.blurb: A wall in the Inner Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, just north of the Dilithium Crystal wall and reached from there. The sixteen routes are mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad pitches, running from 5.8 up to a single low 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Routes are single pitch in a scenic canyon setting, so a single rope and a rack of quickdraws covers most of it. It is a good stop for a party that wants a spread of difficulty without a long day of moving between crags.

ca_south_warm_up_boulder.blurb: A large boulder at the southeast edge of the Shangri-La meadow, in the Tramway area of the San Jacinto Mountains at about 8,500 feet. It holds sixteen problems and is a fine place for beginners or anyone wanting a few more problems: the great majority are VB or V0, with just a couple harder, up to V3. The east face's left edge offers a simple descent. Allow 10 to 15 minutes on foot, heading beyond Frank's Boulder into the rocky drainage higher up; the boulder appears at the meadow's edge as you crest the rise.
